text: The Teke languages are a group of Bantu languages spoken by the Teke people in the western Congo and in Gabon. They are coded Zone B.70 in Guthrie's classification. According to Nurse & Philippson, the Teke languages apart from West Teke form a valid node with Tende

title: Teke-Tyee Language (TYX) – L1 & L2 Speakers... | Ethnologue Free
text: Teke-Tyee is a stable indigenous language of Congo. It belongs to the Niger-Congo language family. The language is used as a first language by all in the ethnic community. It is not known to be taught in schools.
